title: Benchmarking: load baseline configs + stamp runtime build metadata into benchmark outputs
author: Marcus Reed
release_notes: Benchmark outputs now include stamped runtime build + environment metadata (git SHA, build ID, CUDA/driver, GPU SKU, seeds) to improve reproducibility.
Baseline runner can load versioned configs from a locked suite directory or explicit config bundle, and records the resolved config hash in artifacts.
body:
Title: Benchmarking: load baseline configs + stamp runtime build metadata into benchmark outputs

Context
We are locking Q1’26 perf baselines and need benchmark artifacts that are self-describing and reproducible. Today, results JSON tells us p50/p95/p99/TTFT/TPOT, but we frequently have to chase down the exact runtime build, CUDA/driver, and config knobs that produced it (especially when rerunning across regions/fleet pools). This PR introduces (1) a baseline config loader that resolves the exact config bundle used and (2) metadata stamping into every benchmark output artifact.

What’s in this PR
1) Baseline config loader
- Adds a small library to resolve benchmark configs from:
  a) `--baseline-suite-dir` (versioned suite checkout) + `--workload <name>`
  b) `--config <path>` (explicit config file)
  c) `--config-bundle <tar.gz>` (artifact produced by perf-canary)
- Resolution is deterministic and records:
  - `config_source` (suite-dir | config-path | bundle)
  - `resolved_config_path`
  - `resolved_config_sha256`
  - `suite_version` (if present: `suite.toml` / `SUITE_VERSION`)
- Validation: fails fast if required keys are missing (traffic shape name, model id, quant profile, warmup policy).

2) Runtime build metadata stamping
- Every benchmark run now stamps `build_metadata` into the top-level output JSON and per-trial JSON:
  - `runtime_git_sha`
  - `runtime_git_dirty` (boolean)
  - `runtime_version` (from build)
  - `build_id` (CI build number when present)
  - `build_timestamp_utc`
  - `compiler` (clang/gcc) and `build_type` (release/debug)
- Stamps environment details required for cross-run comparisons:
  - `cuda_version` (runtime)
  - `nvidia_driver_version`
  - `gpu_name` + `gpu_uuid` (optional, when accessible)
  - `host_kernel` and `os_release`
  - `container_image` (if set via env)
- Stamps benchmark determinism inputs:
  - `benchmark_seed` (runner)
  - `autotune_seed` (if set)
  - `scheduler_policy_hash` (hash of relevant scheduler flags)

3) Artifact schema changes
- Extends benchmark output schema by adding:
  - `metadata` (config + build + environment) at the top level
  - `metadata.schema_version = 2`
- Backward compatibility:
  - Existing consumers can continue reading metrics fields unchanged.
  - New fields are additive; the runner continues to emit legacy `run_info` fields for one release cycle.

Motivation / why now
- We’re seeing variance investigations blocked on “what build was this?” (esp. driver/CUDA drift and subtle scheduler flag changes). This change makes artifacts self-contained and is required for regression gates to produce actionable diffs.
- Aligns with the baseline artifact lock goals (ENG-4823) and nightly execution (ENG-4827).

Implementation notes
- Build metadata stamping is implemented in `runtime/common/build_info.*` and plumbed through the benchmark runner via `BenchmarkContext`.
- CUDA/driver version detection uses `cudaRuntimeGetVersion` and `nvidia-smi` fallback when available; failure to detect is non-fatal but recorded as `unknown` with an `errors[]` entry.
- SHA256 of resolved configs is computed after normalization (line endings + stripping comments for TOML/YAML) to reduce cross-platform noise.

How to test
Local:
- `./bazel run //bench:runner -- --config benchmarks/configs/llama3_70b_chat_streaming.toml --output out.json --seed 123`
- Verify `metadata.runtime_git_sha` is set and `resolved_config_sha256` is stable across runs.
CI:
- Bench smoke job now asserts `metadata.schema_version == 2` and that required metadata keys are present.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- perf-canary: attach `config_bundle.tar.gz` in run artifacts and have it use `--config-bundle` (tracked in ENG-4827).
- dashboard ingestion: add metadata fields to drilldown pages (owner: Observability pack).

Screenshots / output sample (truncated)
Output JSON now begins with: {"metadata": {"schema_version": 2, "runtime_git_sha": "8f1c7a9...", "cuda_version": "12.4", "nvidia_driver_version": "550.54", "resolved_config_sha256": "a9d2..."}, "metrics": {"ttft_ms_p95": ...}}

Review conversation
- Rina Kobayashi: “Config hashing: are we hashing raw file bytes or normalized config? We’ve been bitten by comment-only diffs.”
  - Marcus Reed: “Normalized. Strips comments + normalizes line endings; added unit tests for TOML/YAML. Raw hash is also included as `resolved_config_sha256_raw` when `--debug-metadata` is set.”
- Logan Wright: “Please make sure we don’t accidentally stamp PII/hostnames into artifacts that get copied around.”
  - Marcus Reed: “Agreed. Hostname is not included; only OS/kernel versions and GPU identifiers (UUID optional and can be disabled via `--redact-hardware-ids`).”
- Nadia Rahman: “Schema change needs a version bump and a clear compatibility story for the pipeline.”
  - Marcus Reed: “Added `metadata.schema_version = 2` and kept legacy `run_info` for one release cycle. Also added a small `schema_migrations.md` entry.”
- Sean Gallagher: “For variance investigations we need the driver/CUDA capture to be best-effort, not a hard failure.”
  - Marcus Reed: “Implemented as best-effort; runner continues and records `metadata.errors[]` for missing values.”
- Connor O'Brien: “Release qualification wants a single field to identify the exact runtime build used.”
  - Marcus Reed: “Added `build_fingerprint = <git_sha>-<build_id>-<build_type>` to simplify.”

CI status
- buildkite/redwood: bazel-build (pass)
- buildkite/redwood: unit-tests (pass)
- buildkite/redwood: benchmark-smoke (pass)
- lint/format (pass)

Merge
- Merged via squash to `main`.
- Squash commit message: “Benchmarking: baseline config loader + build metadata stamping (schema v2)”
